title: Avoid hardcoded credentials
description: Passwords, API keys, and secrets must never appear as string literals in source code. Use environment variables or a secrets manager.

title: Validate and sanitise all external input
description: All data from users, files, or networks must be validated before use. Lack of validation leads to injection and type-confusion defects.

title: Handle exceptions and return error codes explicitly
description: Functions should not silently ignore exceptions. Unhandled exceptions can crash embedded systems or leave them in undefined states.

title: Avoid use of eval() and exec()
description: Dynamic code execution functions can execute arbitrary code injected by an attacker. Prefer explicit logic or safe parsers.

title: Avoid shell injection via subprocess
description: Passing shell=True with user-controlled strings to subprocess functions allows command injection. Use a list of arguments instead.

title: All variables must be initialised before use
description: MISRA C:2012 Rule 9.1 — Objects should not be read before being written. Uninitialised variables cause undefined behaviour.
source: MISRA C:2012 Rule 9.1 (reference only — not a certified citation)

title: Avoid dynamic memory allocation in safety-critical paths
description: MISRA C:2012 Rule 21.3 — malloc/free should not be used in safety-critical software due to fragmentation and non-determinism.
source: MISRA C:2012 Rule 21.3 (reference only — not a certified citation)

title: Limit recursion depth; prefer iterative implementations
description: MISRA C:2012 Rule 17.2 — Recursive functions shall not be used. Recursion makes stack depth hard to bound in embedded systems.
source: MISRA C:2012 Rule 17.2 (reference only — not a certified citation)

title: Verify return values of safety-critical function calls
description: ISO 26262 Part 6 — All results of functions in safety paths must be checked. Ignoring return values can mask faults.
source: ISO 26262:2018 Part 6 (reference only — not a certified citation)

title: Use time-out mechanisms for all blocking operations
description: Blocking calls without timeouts can cause deadlock in real-time vehicle systems. Always specify a maximum wait duration.
source: ISO 26262:2018 Part 6 (reference only — not a certified citation)

title: Protect shared resources with appropriate synchronisation
description: ISO/SAE 21434 and ISO 26262 — Race conditions in shared data structures can lead to safety and security faults.
source: ISO 26262:2018 Part 6 / ISO/SAE 21434:2021 (reference only — not a certified citation)

title: Implement secure boot and integrity checks
description: ISO/SAE 21434 — ECU firmware must be verified before execution to prevent tampering. Use cryptographic signatures.
source: ISO/SAE 21434:2021 (reference only — not a certified citation)

title: Limit CAN/bus message trust: validate sender and content
description: Vehicle bus messages must not be blindly trusted. Validate message IDs, lengths, and checksums before acting on them.
source: ISO/SAE 21434:2021 (reference only — not a certified citation)

title: Use strong, well-reviewed cryptographic algorithms
description: Avoid MD5, SHA-1, DES, or custom cryptography. Use AES-256, SHA-256/SHA-3, and established TLS libraries.

title: Sanitise path inputs to prevent directory traversal
description: File paths built from user input must be validated. Directory traversal can expose or overwrite sensitive files.

title: Use parameterised queries; never concatenate SQL strings
description: String concatenation in SQL queries leads to injection. Use prepared statements or ORM query builders.
